title: Best early drummers: Cantrell and D.D. Chandler
summary: He names Cantrell and Chandler as the best drummers of his boyhood, says Chandler needed to be half high, and that he copied Chandler's style and walk.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Who were some of the best bands when you were a boy? Who did you hear? Who were the best drummers you heard when you were a little boy?
When I was a boy, just learning. Little boy.
Yeah, the smallest you can remember, as far back as you can remember. Who were the best drummers in the old days?
Well, the best drummers was Cantrap. And they had another drummer they called Edie Chandler.
Did he play on the street too, or just on the street? On the street. On the street.
On the street. And Edie Chandler, he couldn't play unless he was half high.
He'd get high. He was getting high.
Yeah, he'd drink it. Did he always play snare drum or bass drum sometime on the parade? He played snare. Snare.

That's how I'm going to play a snare drum. I used to sing when I was a boy. I used to second line. And I always just said I wanted to play a small drum in the brass band. And I adopted his style. And I adopted how he wascapped and walked. And I'd do the same thing.
Did he play a lot of roles, or would he play like what? Huh? Did he play a lot of drum rolls, or what style did he play?

Yeah, he played a lot of roles and everything. D.D. Chandler and Cantrell, the drummer and the drum, and the maker, it sounded like it would turn a piece of cloth. Well, see, those fellas used sharp drums. All good. Tuned it up high, you mean, had it up tight or what?
